closes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/9210

pr_comments: You can iterate backwards through an array.
I am not a fan of this change. I have already found buggy recording rules and federation issues thanks to this error message. This would need more thinking from my side.

> This would need more thinking from my side.

+1. Thinking about it more, I feel wrong sending no error. Silently discarding duplicate samples might prevent/delay detecting some bugs.

While keeping the Prometheus behaviour same, I think we could instead provide a helper function to check if the samples matches last 4 samples, that Cortex or any other vendor could use.

The source of this PR/issue was an issue between `Prometheus-remote-write <-> Remote-storage` interaction, and the remote write stage would already assure that the sample that it is sending is not actually a duplicate as it has been through Prometheus which has a check for it, so it feels safe and sensible to have solution for this in the Remote storage. Having it here will interfere with Prometheus' interaction with scrapers and rules and detection of bugs.

cc @bboreham

>so it feels safe and sensible to have solution for this in the Remote storage

cmiiw, what you are proposing is to not hardcode the checking of last 4 samples, but to expose a utility function that the individual remote storage can choose to use and which checks if the new sample is a duplicate of the last 4 already received?

@darshanime I am not sure why we would need to touch anything beyond the `tsdb` package. Maybe there is some misunderstanding. When I say a utility function, it is just a Go function that other vendors can use it via their tsdb import. Where and how this function goes is still a TBD before we implement it.

Also, I would like to avoid any interface extensions for this, so I am looking at a method for the Head that takes `(series ref, series labels, timestamp, value)` and returns our desired result. @bboreham I think this should be enough to check "if this sample for this series matches any of last 4 samples".
thanks for the clarification, i've made the changes 👍

Digging this up during our bug scrub.

@bboreham , you closed the issue this PR is addressing. ("This is no longer true, so it's not a simple proposal any longer. Closing.") We assume that means that the approach in this PR isn't valid anymore, but we aren't sure. What do you think?
Yes, Prometheus no longer has the 4 values, so this PR cannot go ahead.

issue_context.title: Allow duplicate samples matching last 4
issue_context.body:
When using remote-write, it may happen that a write request is received, but the sender does not receive the acknowledgement and re-sends it.

Currently Prometheus checks if a sample duplicates the last one received, and silently discards the duplicate (returns nil) in that case:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/bb05485c79084fecd3602eceafca3d554ab88987/tsdb/head_append.go#L296-L301

However a remote-write sender may lag several scrapes behind, and include multiple samples in each send.
So we may receive a duplicate of the second-last sample received, or earlier.

I think it requires some coincidences, because to get a duplicate in the default-size send of 500 samples implies that only 250 series are being sent on that shard, but with high numbers of shards, much bigger send size, or just some luck with the hashing, it would happen.

## Proposal
We have the last 4 samples in `s.sampleBuf`, so we could check all of them for a match.
comments: I am not clear what we are trying to achieve. Duplicate sample means the value changes while timestamp is same, and Prometheus remote writing won't cause that, it will be the same value. It will mostly have out of order samples from what you just described.
I mean to return nil if the timestamp and value are an exact match of one of the last four received.

So basically do not send "out of order" if it is within the last 4 samples. I have seen out of order messages regularly with remote write because of the issue that you mentioned, so this check for last 4 samples should be acceptable iff it is a exact match.

> I have seen out of order messages regularly with remote write

Yeah, me too; I'm trying to figure out how they come about.

> because of the issue that you mentioned

I still struggle to believe this particular cause is common.  Maybe I got the math wrong?
I have removed help wanted and low hanging fruit as it turns out it might not be that straighforward.

> We have the last 4 samples in s.sampleBuf, so we could check all of them for a match.

This is no longer true, so it's not a simple proposal any longer.  Closing.
